gaps.sentence: Visitors ___ wear badges at all times inside the plant.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' = a rule that has to be followed.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.

gaps.sentence: We ___ have hurried — the concert was cancelled anyway.
gaps.hint: the rush turned out to be unnecessary
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't have hurried' means we hurried although it was unnecessary: needn't have.

gaps.sentence: I ___ see the sea from my bedroom window when I was little.
gaps.explanation: Verbs of perception use 'could' for past ability: could see.

gaps.sentence: Her car is not in the car park and her office light is off, so she ___ home.
gaps.hint: a confident conclusion about the past
gaps.explanation: A confident conclusion about the past uses 'must have' plus the participle: must have gone.

gaps.sentence: ___ I borrow your charger for a minute?
gaps.explanation: 'May' is the polite way to ask permission: May I borrow.

gaps.sentence: You ___ worry — I have already sent the invitations.
gaps.explanation: 'Needn't' reassures someone that an action is unnecessary: needn't worry.

gaps.sentence: When I was a child, I ___ stay up late on New Year's Eve.
gaps.hint: permission that existed in the past
gaps.explanation: 'Was allowed to' expresses past permission; 'could' is also possible: was allowed to.
